**22 palavras novas** (análises).

blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C1):** eu consigo usar orações relativas avançadas (whose, the results of which, in which, which = a oração inteira) em uma resenha.

body: Esta aula treina **ouvir e anotar informações (IELTS Listening, TOEFL Listening)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.title: Review: “The Numbers Behind the News”
paras: This is a book **whose** author clearly loves data. Its first chapter, **in which** she dissects a famous headline, is the best; the figures **on which** the headline relied turn out to be flawed. Her case studies, **the results of which** are summarized in tables, are clear.

The book has one weakness, **which** is repetition. Readers **who** know statistics may skim; those **for whom** the subject is new will benefit most. A scientist **to whom** I lent my copy called it “essential”.

items.q: The first chapter dissects a famous headline.
The book’s weakness is its price.

head: Estrutura
Exemplo
rows: a chapter **in which** she dissects…; people **for whom** it is new
tables, **the results of which** are clear
The book repeats itself, **which** is its weakness.
figures **relied on** → figures **on which** it relied

blocks.body: Em registro formal, a preposição vem **antes** de *which/whom*: *the data on which the claim rests*. **Whose** indica posse e serve para pessoas e coisas. Com vírgulas = não restritiva.
✗ *the man who’s book* → ✓ *the man whose book*. Depois de preposição, *that* e *who* não funcionam: ✗ *in that she*.

items.s: The chapter in ___ she dissects a headline is the best. (which)
Readers for ___ the subject is new will benefit. (whom)
The book repeats itself, ___ is its weakness. (which)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

items.ans: Which chapter did you like best
items.pt: De qual capítulo você mais gostou?

body: **on which the claim rests** — sobre o qual a afirmação se apoia
**the extent to which** — a medida em que
**a case in point** — um exemplo claro
**a point on which we agree** — um ponto em que concordamos
**whose idea it was** — de quem foi a ideia
**for whom it matters** — para quem importa
**of which more later** — sobre o qual mais adiante
**in which case,…** — nesse caso,…
**Which chapter did you like best?** — De qual capítulo você mais gostou?
**And the weakness?** — E a fraqueza?
**It repeats itself, which is tiring.** — Repete-se, o que cansa.

items.label: Pausas e ritmo
items.note: Ênfase intencional: a palavra mais importante da frase recebe o acento mais forte e a nota mais alta, para marcar contraste ou correção.
words: It was the POLICY, not the person.
We need MORE time, not more money.

prompts.model: It is a book whose author loves data.
The chapter in which she explains it is the best.

prompts.q: Use which for the whole clause.
prompts.model: It repeats itself, which is its weakness.

blocks.task: Write 5 sentences about a book or film using whose, in which, of which, for whom and sentence-which.
blocks.model: It is a film whose director grew up in the town. The final scene, in which the family reunites, is moving. The cast, most of whom are amateurs, is superb. It is aimed at viewers for whom the story is new. It runs three hours, which is too long.

items.why: **case study table** = tabela de estudo de caso.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
